standard_prerequisites.use: Case 3: excludes an abstraction reading of a term beginning with a parenthesis followed by a non-abstraction head.

standard_prerequisites.use: Case 2: an abstraction cannot also be built as an application.

standard_prerequisites.name: No proper initial part of a term is a term
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same unit, \ollabel{lem:initial} (statement at source line 1569; the unit leaves its proof as an exercise by induction on length)
standard_prerequisites.use: Case 3: two application readings would force one first argument to be a proper initial segment of the other.

core_obligations: Variable case (proof lines 1582-1586): abstractions and applications always start with a parenthesis, so a bare variable admits only the variable rule.
Abstraction case (lines 1587-1593): not a variable by shape, not an application by the app-start lemma, hence an abstraction over N, whose own formation is unique by the induction hypothesis.

Application case (lines 1594-1606): the term-start lemma rules out an abstraction reading; a second application reading (P'Q') makes P a proper initial segment of P' or vice versa, impossible by the initial-segment lemma; both immediate subterms are unique by the induction hypothesis.
proof_roadmap: Induct on the formation of M.
Separate the three shapes by their opening symbols using the start lemmas.
Rule out double readings in the application case via the no-proper-initial-part lemma.
Apply the induction hypothesis to the subterms.
difficulty_reason: Unique readability for the formal grammar of terms (statement 1574-1578, proof 1580-1607): three fully written induction cases glued together by three small shape lemmas of the same section. The proof itself delegates nothing; one of its citations (lem:initial) is a stated lemma whose own proof the textbook leaves as an exercise, noted in the prerequisites. H2: standard syntactic induction with all cases explicit.
